topics.label: Introduction and lecture learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture series, identifies its audience and sets out the learning outcomes.

topics.label: Cancer development and the importance of tissue context
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the transformation of normal cells into cancer cells as a disruption of differentiation that must be understood within tissue architecture.

topics.label: Distinguishing benign and malignant tumours through invasion and metastasis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish how local invasion and distant spread distinguish malignant tumours from contained benign growths.

topics.label: Benign tumour progression and clinical risks
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the clinical significance of benign tumours, showing how some progress to invasive cancer while others can cause harm without becoming malignant.

topics.label: Tumour nomenclature
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how tumour names indicate tissue of origin and malignant status, including exceptions to the naming conventions.

topics.label: How cancer causes illness and death
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how tumour growth and metastatic spread disrupt normal bodily functions and cause morbidity and mortality.

topics.label: Tumour incidence in humans and other animals
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics compare the frequency and distribution of tumour types across human populations and animal species.

topics.label: Cancer detection and screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain why early cancer detection is difficult and evaluate screening approaches according to their ability to identify treatable disease.

topics.label: Lecture close and upcoming practicals
topics.groupedBecause: This closing returns to the learning outcomes and directs students towards revision and upcoming teaching sessions.
